points.description: States the purpose: both RPF and RPB broadcast more efficiently than flooding by minimizing duplicate packets, AND explains how RPF works: a node X receiving a packet from sender S via neighbor N consults its unicast routing table and forwards the packet to all adjacent nodes (except N) only if it would itself send packets to S via N (i.e., the packet arrived over the best route); otherwise it discards it.
points.partial_credit: Award 0.5 if only the purpose (fewer duplicates than flooding) or only the RPF forwarding mechanism is correctly given.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both the purpose (reducing duplicates versus flooding) and the RPF mechanism (forward only if the packet arrived from the neighbor used to reach the source, based on the routing table). Only one of the two earns half. Equivalent wording is accepted.
